shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with the eschatological formula בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַיָּמִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.2.2, byte tier), “It shall happen in the latter days” (web:Isa.2.2), introducing an unconditional promise of the nations streaming to Yahweh's house and universal peace, distinct in mode from the header it follows. The row closes at “They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.” (web:Isa.2.4), where a petuchah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.2.4, single-witness, tier-3), before the imperative vocative that opens verse 5.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the row through verse 5 to include “House of Jacob, come, and let's walk in the light of Yahweh.” (web:Isa.2.5) as a closing exhortation was rejected because a petuchah break is recorded at the close of verse 4 (oshb:Isa.2.4, single-witness, tier-3), and verse 5's imperative opens a fresh address rather than continuing the oracle's own eschatological description.

shipped_row.device_notes: The oracle names “the house of the God of Jacob” (web:Isa.2.3), a catchword shared with verse 5's “House of Jacob” (web:Isa.2.5) that could argue for reading 2-5 as one bracketed unit; the petuchah break at verse 4 is preferred here as the stronger, more local disclosure signal.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The row is bounded to the single ha-davar header verse: הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.2.1, byte tier), “This is what Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.” (web:Isa.2.1). Unlike the chazon header at 1:1, this header opens with the noun ‘the word’ (ha-davar) rather than ‘the vision’ (chazon), a distinct header-noun class naming the same seer and Judah/Jerusalem object; it carries no imperative or address of its own, and verse 2 opens a fresh eschatological formula (“It shall happen in the latter days”, web:Isa.2.2), which is the row's own seam. Immediately upstream of that seam, 1:31 closes with a setumah break of its own (oshb:Isa.1.31, single-witness, tier-3), corroborating the division from the chapter that precedes it.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 2:1 into the following mountain-of-the-house oracle was rejected because the header verse names no imperative or eschatological content of its own, unlike the material that follows it.
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: The header-noun contrast with 1:1 (davar vs. chazon) is a genuine lexical distinction, not a copying variant. The two superscriptions also share three recurring elements at three different tiers: the relative clause אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה collates at byte tier (oshb:Isa.1.1 tokens 5-6; oshb:Isa.2.1 tokens 2-3), the strongest of the three; the seer's name יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ / יְשַֽׁעְיָ֖הוּ collates at accent_stripped tier (oshb:Isa.1.1 token 2; oshb:Isa.2.1 token 4); and the patronymic בֶן אָמ֔וֹץ / בֶּן אָמ֑וֹץ collates at skeleton tier only, the construct form's dagesh and the name's accent both differing (oshb:Isa.1.1 tokens 3-4; oshb:Isa.2.1 tokens 5-6).

next_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with the imperative-vocative בֵּ֖ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב לְכ֥וּ וְנֵלְכָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.2.5, byte tier), “House of Jacob, come, and let's walk in the light of Yahweh.” (web:Isa.2.5), reusing the ‘Jacob’ catchword from the preceding oracle as a hook while opening its own address. The row runs through the description of pride, idolatry, and the coming terror of Yahweh, closing on the refrain-clause וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא (oshb:Isa.2.11, byte tier), “Yahweh alone will be exalted in that day.” (oshb:Isa.2.11), where a setumah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.2.11, single-witness, tier-3); the row's own opening seam carries a mark too, a petuchah closing verse 4 (oshb:Isa.2.4, single-witness, tier-3) just before it. The identical clause recurs verbatim at 2:17 (byte tier, collated against both sites, sweep: 2 verses), closing a parallel second stanza and arguing that the refrain brackets each stanza rather than the whole 2:5-22 complex.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 2:5-22 as one unbroken oracle was rejected because the closing refrain clause recurs byte-identically at 2:11 and 2:17, arguing that the refrain closes two shorter stanzas rather than leaving the whole complex uncut, on the same bracket-closing logic used for repeated refrains elsewhere in the book; the flight-from-terror motif that recurs from 2:10 into 2:19 and 2:21 (accent_stripped tier; sweep: 3 verses) does not disturb this division either, since its two later sites lie beyond the present stanza and argue only at complex level, not against this stanza's own closing bracket.

next_row.device_notes: Verse 6's second-person accusation (“you have forsaken your people, the house of Jacob”, web:Isa.2.6), נָטַ֗שְׁתָּה עַמְּךָ֙ (oshb:Isa.2.6, tokens 2-3, a 2ms perfect with a 2ms suffix), leaves its grammatical addressee ambiguous in the Hebrew; this construal question is held open and not resolved by the row. The refrain's own ‘loftiness of man’ clause varies in word order between 2:11 and 2:17 (form variant, not byte-identical); only the closing ‘Yahweh alone… in that day’ clause is byte-identical at both sites. A flight-from-terror motif crosses the row's own closing seam: the four-token core מִפְּנֵי֙ פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֔ה וּמֵהֲדַ֖ר (oshb:Isa.2.10) recurs at oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21, accent_stripped tier across the three sites (sweep: 3 verses); the later two share a byte-identical eight-token run (מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ, sweep: 2 verses, byte), while the earlier site's majesty noun is defective against the plene spelling at the later two. A low/bow root chain also runs through the stanza: וַיִּשְׁפַּל (oshb:Isa.2.9), וְשַׁ֖ח (oshb:Isa.2.11), וְשָׁפֵֽל (oshb:Isa.2.12), and וְשַׁח֙ (oshb:Isa.2.17), standing at 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton).

next_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with the Day-of-Yahweh formula כִּ֣י י֞וֹם לַיהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת (oshb:Isa.2.12, byte tier), “For there will be a day of Yahweh of Armies” (web:Isa.2.12), a fresh temporal-formula onset launching the catalogue of high and lofty things (cedars, oaks, mountains, towers, ships, imagery) that closes on the same refrain clause as the preceding stanza, וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא (oshb:Isa.2.17, byte tier), “Yahweh alone shall be exalted in that day.” (web:Isa.2.17). Verse 11, right before this row starts, is itself setumah-marked (oshb:Isa.2.11, single-witness, tier-3), the same mark disclosed as the closing witness for the stanza it ends.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the high-things catalogue (2:13-16) from its opening formula (2:12) and closing refrain (2:17) into separate rows was rejected because the catalogue is a single polysyndetic (waw-coordinated) list: the preposition עַ֥ל/וְעַ֖ל governing the quantifier כָּל as its object recurs eight times across 2:13-16, matching the governing verse's own two-part coordination at oshb:Isa.2.12 (עַ֥ל כָּל גֵּאֶ֖ה וָרָ֑ם without the conjunction, וְעַ֖ל כָּל נִשָּׂ֥א וְשָׁפֵֽל with it), not a self-standing unit, read here as enumeration inside its governing oracle rather than a separate row.

next_row.device_notes: The cedar/oak/mountain/tower/ship catalogue (2:13-16) is enumeration inside this unit, not an independent list register; polysyndetic (waw-coordinated) inventory catalogues of this kind are read as texture inside their governing oracle here, not as a unit on its own. The row's own opening seam carries cross-seam cohesion: oshb:Isa.2.12 opens with כִּ֣י (oshb:Isa.2.12), the same particle that opens oshb:Isa.2.6 inside the preceding stanza's own span (web:Isa.2.5-Isa.2.11), both witnesses rendering it as subordinating there. The low/bow root runs unbroken across the seam and through the stanza — וַיִּשְׁפַּל (oshb:Isa.2.9), שָׁפֵ֔ל וְשַׁ֖ח (oshb:Isa.2.11), וְשָׁפֵֽל (oshb:Isa.2.12) — standing at 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton), and it interleaves at 2:12-14 with the paired high/lofty vocabulary that the row's own catalogue enumerates (הָרָמִ֖ים וְהַנִּשָּׂאִ֑ים at oshb:Isa.2.13, הָרָמִ֑ים / הַנִּשָּׂאֽוֹת at oshb:Isa.2.14), closing again with וְשַׁח֙ גַּבְה֣וּת הָאָדָ֔ם וְשָׁפֵ֖ל at oshb:Isa.2.17. That link leaves a live rival unstated: one sustained pride-and-humbling poem running from 2:9 through 2:17, with the refrain as internal punctuation rather than a row-cutting seam.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with וְהָאֱלִילִ֖ים כָּלִ֥יל יַחֲלֹֽף (oshb:Isa.2.18, byte tier), “The idols shall utterly pass away.” (web:Isa.2.18), moving from the refrain-closed catalogue of proud things to the idols' own fate and humanity's flight into caves and holes, a fresh topical turn after the stanza-closing refrain of verse 17. The row runs through the closing exhortation “Stop trusting in man, whose breath is in his nostrils; for of what account is he?” (oshb:Isa.2.22), where a petuchah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.2.22, single-witness, tier-3) at the chapter's end.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 2:18-22 as a third refrain-bounded stanza of the same shape as 2:5-11 and 2:12-17 was rejected because no closing ‘Yahweh alone… in that day’ clause recurs at its end; the unit is bounded instead by topical shift (from proud objects to idols and human flight) and the petuchah break closing the chapter.

prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 2:18-22 as a third refrain-bounded stanza of the same shape as 2:5-11 and 2:12-17 was rejected because no closing ‘Yahweh alone… in that day’ clause recurs at its end; the unit is bounded instead by topical shift (from proud objects to idols and human flight) and the petuchah break closing the chapter.

prev_row.device_notes: The ‘in that day’ temporal tag recurs at verse 20 (web:Isa.2.20), continuing the temporal frame of the refrain-closed stanzas without reopening the refrain clause itself. A flight-from-terror motif straddles the row's own opening seam: the four-token core מִפְּנֵי֙ פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֔ה וּמֵהֲדַ֖ר recurs at oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 within this row, with a third site further upstream at oshb:Isa.2.10, accent_stripped tier across the three (sweep: 3 verses). Within the row, the two in-span sites share a longer eight-token run, מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ, byte-identical between oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 2 verses, byte).

next_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with the explicit legal-summons formula נִצָּ֥ב לָרִ֖יב יְהוָ֑ה וְעֹמֵ֖ד לָדִ֥ין עַמִּֽים (oshb:Isa.3.13, byte tier), “Yahweh stands up to contend, and stands to judge the peoples.” (web:Isa.3.13), the contend-infinitive לָרִ֖יב (token 2) standing at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton, token-exact) and the judge-infinitive לָדִ֥ין (token 5) at exactly 1 (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton, token-exact), so the pairing cannot recur anywhere else in the book, addressed to “the elders of his people and their leaders” (web:Isa.3.14), a distinct addressee from the general my-people material of the preceding unit. The row closes on the postpositive signature נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Isa.3.15, byte tier), “says the Lord, Yahweh of Armies.” (oshb:Isa.3.15), where a setumah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.3.15, single-witness, tier-3; the verse also carries a ketiv/qere note not engaged by this quoted signature clause), before the fresh vayomer narrative onset of verse 16. This same opening seam has its own tier-3 witness: a setumah break closes verse 12 (oshb:Isa.3.12, single-witness) immediately before the row begins.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this row into the preceding leadership-collapse unit (3:1-12) was rejected because verse 13 opens with its own verse-initial legal-summons formula, נִצָּ֥ב לָרִ֖יב יְהוָ֑ה וְעֹמֵ֖ד לָדִ֥ין עַמִּֽים (oshb:Isa.3.13, byte tier), addressed to a distinct addressee (the elders and leaders) rather than continuing the general my-people material. Running the row on to the narrative onset at oshb:Isa.3.16 was also rejected, since that verse opens its own וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה narrative formula (the verse also carries a ketiv/qere note later in its own line, not engaged by this quoted onset), a distinct frame class from the postpositive neum signature closing this row at verse 15.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens on the book’s first sung-frame onset, the cohortative "אָשִׁ֤ירָה נָּא֙ לִֽידִידִ֔י שִׁירַ֥ת דּוֹדִ֖י לְכַרְמ֑וֹ כֶּ֛רֶם הָיָ֥ה לִֽידִידִ֖י בְּקֶ֥רֶן בֶּן שָֽׁמֶן" (oshb:Isa.5.1, byte tier), matching WEB’s “Let me sing for my well beloved a song of my beloved about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a very fruitful hill.” (web:Isa.5.1) -- a tier-1 addressee/genre shift from the preceding oracle. The love-song frame is then read forensically: the summons “Now, inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, please judge between me and my vineyard. What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it? Why, when I looked for it to yield grapes, did it yield wild grapes?” (web:Isa.5.3-Isa.5.4) puts Jerusalem and Judah in the juror’s seat, and the unit closes with the vineyard’s explicit identification and verdict, sealed by the sound-play "וַיְקַ֤ו לְמִשְׁפָּט֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִשְׂפָּ֔ח לִצְדָקָ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה צְעָקָֽה" (oshb:Isa.5.7, byte tier), rendered “For the vineyard of Yahweh of Armies is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant. He looked for justice, but behold, oppression, for righteousness, but behold, a cry of distress.” (web:Isa.5.7). The next verse breaks to a differently-addressed class (land monopolists) under a fresh hoy onset (web:Isa.5.8), a clean tier-1 seam.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative keeps the vineyard song bound to the following hoy verse as one merged indictment, but web:Isa.5.8 opens a distinct addressee class (land-grabbing landowners, not the vineyard-as-Israel figure) under its own verse-initial hoy onset, arguing a fresh unit rather than a continuation.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: juridical vineyard song read as forensic indictment
shipped_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
shipped_row.device_notes: Though staged in the "שִׁירַ֥ת" (oshb:Isa.5.1, byte tier) song-frame construct, the unit’s function is forensic indictment, not sung praise; it is categorized judgment_oracle under the operative-category law rather than hymn_doxology, with the genre-blend disclosed here. The verdict names the vineyard as "כֶ֜רֶם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙" (oshb:Isa.5.7, byte tier), the-vineyard-of-YHWH-of-Armies construct, read alongside WEB’s “the vineyard of Yahweh of Armies is the house of Israel” (web:Isa.5.7). A tier-3 parashah witness marks a petuchah at oshb:Isa.4.6; and a setumah at oshb:Isa.5.7; this is single-witness corroboration, disclosed for symmetry, and it did not drive this boundary.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with the temporal-formula turn בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶה֙ צֶ֣מַח יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.4.2, byte tier), “In that day, Yahweh's branch will be beautiful and glorious” (web:Isa.4.2), an unconditional promise sharply reversing the preceding judgment unit's mood. The row runs through the verse pairing two distinct roots in synonymous parallelism, הַנִּשְׁאָ֣ר (the book's four-way remnant-family root) and וְהַנּוֹתָר֙ (a different root, the one opening oshb:Isa.1.8) (oshb:Isa.4.3, byte tier at each), “he who is left in Zion and he who remains in Jerusalem” (oshb:Isa.4.3), and closes on the pavilion image “a pavilion for a shade in the daytime from the heat” (oshb:Isa.4.6), where a petuchah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.4.6, single-witness, tier-3) at the chapter's close. The row's own opening seam carries a mark too: a setumah break closes verse 4:1 (oshb:Isa.4.1, single-witness, tier-3) just before it.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 4:2-6 to the preceding daughters-of-Zion unit as its eventual outcome was rejected because verse 2's temporal formula introduces an unconditional promise in a wholly different register from the judgment material it follows, a sharp mode shift read as the row's own opening seam.
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: The pavilion noun sukkah at the row's close, וְסֻכָּ֛ה (oshb:Isa.4.6, token 1, a vav-conjunction prefix), shares its bare consonantal root with the sukkah figure describing the besieged daughter of Zion at 1:8, כְּסֻכָּ֣ה (oshb:Isa.1.8, token 4, a kaf-preposition prefix) — as prefixed tokens the two forms collate at no tier; stripped of their prefixes the bare nouns match at accent_stripped tier, and once the noun's own homograph is excluded the object stands at exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 6 verses, skeleton, of which 4 are the excluded homograph), a reversal-echo bracketing the besieged-daughter image that opens the book (1:8) and the shelter image that closes this unit (4:6), disclosed here rather than argued as a row boundary. The referent of ‘Yahweh's branch’ (web:Isa.4.2) is not decided by this row. The opening temporal formula also straddles the row's own opening seam at less than byte tier: בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ (oshb:Isa.4.1) stands mid-verse at tokens 6-7 against בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.4.2) verse-initial at tokens 1-2, accent_stripped tier; the formula recurs densely nearby (sweep: 7 verses across chapters 2-4, 45 verses book-wide, skeleton) and is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.3.18 too, where it continues the same judgment material as enumeration rather than opening a seam, and what discriminates the two uses is the register shift: at 3:18 the formula introduces a further removal-item inside the same judgment oracle, while at 4:2 it introduces an unconditional salvation promise reversing that judgment mood, which is why only the latter carries the row's own opening seam.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh verse-initial hoy opens the row: "ה֗וֹי מַגִּיעֵ֥י בַ֨יִת֙ בְּבַ֔יִת שָׂדֶ֥ה בְשָׂדֶ֖ה יַקְרִ֑יבוּ עַ֚ד אֶ֣פֶס מָק֔וֹם וְהֽוּשַׁבְתֶּ֥ם לְבַדְּכֶ֖ם בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ" (oshb:Isa.5.8, byte tier), matching WEB’s “Woe to those who join house to house, who lay field to field, until there is no room, and you are made to dwell alone in the middle of the land!” (web:Isa.5.8) -- the first of the chapter’s six hoy onsets (sweep: 22 verses book-wide; six verse-initial here). The indictment of land monopoly runs through its consequence oracle, “In my ears, Yahweh of Armies says: “Surely many houses will be desolate, even great and beautiful, unoccupied. For ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and a homer of seed shall yield an ephah.” (web:Isa.5.9-Isa.5.10), and the next verse’s hoy onset (web:Isa.5.11) opens a new, unrelated vice class, marking the row’s rear seam.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative treats web:Isa.5.9-Isa.5.10 as a separate consequence-oracle row split from the web:Isa.5.8 indictment, but the two are bound by one elliptical oath run whose bytes carry no speech verb of their own, "בְּאָזְנָ֖י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אִם לֹ֞א" (oshb:Isa.5.9, byte tier) -- the rendering’s “says:” supplies the verb the Hebrew leaves implicit -- running without a break and crossing no tier-1 seam, arguing one merged unit.
